summary: Part II of DiamondsAndVStacks, starting after its Layer D6 (pre-adic diamondification, Galois quotient, point map, seminormal rigid full faithfulness). D7 proves that diamondification forgets universal homeomorphisms (SW20 Proposition 10.2.1, under the residue-field hypothesis proved for finite maps) and perfection, and is fully faithful on perfect schemes (SW20 Proposition 18.3.1) and on perfect discrete sources (Gleason Theorem 2.32), with Gleason's olivine spectrum computing |Spd(B, B⁺)|. D8 constructs scheme-theoretic v-sheaves, the reduction functor F ↦ F^red as right adjoint of ⋄, and formally adic, formally closed and formally separated maps. D9 constructs specialization maps of specializing v-sheaves, prekimberlites (formal schemes are examples), formal neighbourhoods, Heuer's thickening and SP_F, and the equivalence of étale formal neighbourhoods with étale perfect schemes over the reduction. D10 recovers flat normal formal schemes locally formally of finite type and proper flat normal schemes over O_E from their v-sheaves (SW20 Proposition 18.4.1, Lourenço's specialization-triple theorem, de Jong's theorem on power-bounded functions), develops v-closures, and proves the flat-closure statement used by Kisin–Pappas–Zhou. D11 develops valuative prekimberlites, smelted kimberlites, kimberlites, tubular neighbourhoods, constructibly Jacobson diamonds, richness and topological normality, proves Gleason's quotient theorem and the connected-components criterion with an explicit closed-specialization hypothesis (Lemmas 4.53, 4.55), and the π-adic kimberlite theory of AGLR §2.3 with its specialization principle.

nodes.title: Finite universal homeomorphisms in characteristic zero preserve completed residue fields
nodes.statement: Let K be a complete nonarchimedean field of characteristic 0 and f : X → X' a finite morphism of adic spaces locally of finite type over Spa(K, K°) that is a universal homeomorphism: every base change of f along a morphism of adic spaces is a homeomorphism. Then for every x ∈ X with image x' = f(x) the map of completed residue fields K(x') → K(x) is an isomorphism of nonarchimedean fields carrying K(x')⁺ onto K(x)⁺.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
f finite: affinoid-locally Spa(B, B⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺) with B finite over A and B⁺ the integral closure of A⁺.
Characteristic 0 makes every finite field extension separable; this is where the hypothesis enters.
proofSteps: Finiteness gives a finite extension K(x)/K(x'), since the residue field of B at a point is a quotient of B ⊗_A κ(x').

Base change along Spa(C, C⁺) → X' with C a completed algebraic closure of K(x') and C⁺ extending K(x')⁺. The reduced geometric fibre over x' is a disjoint union of d copies of Spa(C, C⁺), with d = [K(x):K(x')], by separability. The finite fibre itself can have nilpotents. Universal injectivity forces d = 1.

For a finite morphism the integral valuation subring K(x)⁺ is the integral closure of K(x')⁺ in K(x). Since the field extension has degree one and a valuation ring is integrally closed, the two integral valuation subrings agree.
acceptance: For the normalization t ↦ (t², t³) of the cuspidal cubic over K the unique point above the cusp has residue field K.

The finite morphism Spa(L, O_L) → Spa(K, O_K) for a nontrivial finite extension L/K is surjective and injective but not a universal homeomorphism: after base change to a completed algebraic closure it has [L:K] points.

sources.match: Asserts without proof that in characteristic 0 a universal homeomorphism is the same as a homeomorphism inducing isomorphisms of completed residue fields, with the cuspidal-cubic normalization as example; the finite case is proved here by counting geometric points.

nodes.title: Integral structure sheaves modulo p^n along a residue-preserving homeomorphism
nodes.statement: Let f : X → X' be a morphism of analytic pre-adic spaces over Spa(Q_p, Z_p) that is a homeomorphism and induces, for every x ∈ X, an isomorphism of completed residue fields K(f(x)) → K(x) carrying K(f(x))⁺ onto K(x)⁺. Then for every n ≥ 1 the map O⁺_{X'}/p^n → f_*(O⁺_X/p^n) is an isomorphism of sheaves on |X'| = |X| (quotients taken as sheaves).
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
p is topologically nilpotent on X and X', since both lie over Spa(Q_p, Z_p).
proofSteps: Compare stalks. For a point x of an analytic pre-adic space, the kernel of O⁺_{X,x} → κ(x)⁺ consists of germs g with |g(x)| = 0; each lies in p^n O⁺_{X,x}, because g/p^n is bounded by 1 on the rational neighbourhood {|g| ≤ |p^n|} of x.
Hence O⁺_{X,x}/p^n = κ(x)⁺/p^n = K(x)⁺/p^n, the last since K(x)⁺ is the completion of κ(x)⁺ for a topology in which p is topologically nilpotent.
The hypothesis identifies K(x')⁺/p^n with K(x)⁺/p^n compatibly with the map of stalks, and f is a homeomorphism, so the sheaf map is an isomorphism.
acceptance: For the identity of X the comparison is the identity of O⁺_X/p^n.
For X' = Spa(Q_p, Z_p) and X = Spa(Q_p(√p), Z_p[√p]) the map is a homeomorphism of one-point spaces, the residue fields differ, and Z_p/p → Z_p[√p]/p is not an isomorphism: the hypothesis is needed.

sources.match: States that O⁺_{X'}/p^n → O⁺_X/p^n is an isomorphism of sheaves on |X| = |X'| and checks it on stalks K(x')⁺/p^n → K(x)⁺/p^n using equality of residue fields.

nodes.title: Universal homeomorphisms induce isomorphisms of diamonds
nodes.statement: Let f : X → X' be a morphism of analytic pre-adic spaces over Spa(Q_p, Z_p) which is a homeomorphism and induces isomorphisms of completed residue fields with their valuation subrings (by D7/residue-fields-of-finite-universal-homeomorphisms this holds for every finite universal homeomorphism of adic spaces locally of finite type over a nonarchimedean field over Q_p). Then f^♦ : X^♦ → X'^♦ is an isomorphism of diamonds over Spd Q_p.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).

Scholze–Weinstein state the result for all universal homeomorphisms of analytic pre-adic spaces over Spa Q_p; their reduction to the residue-field condition is the assertion recorded as the gap 'Completed residue fields of a general universal homeomorphism'.
proofSteps: It suffices that for every affinoid perfectoid Y = Spa(S, S⁺) and every Y → X' (with Y the untilt) there is a unique factorization through f.
The underlying map |Y| → |X'| = |X| is given; one needs a map of sheaves |f|*O_X → O_Y compatible with the plus subsheaves.
By D7/plus-sheaf-mod-p-comparison, O⁺_X/p^n = O⁺_{X'}/p^n, giving maps |f|*O⁺_X/p^n → O⁺_Y/p^n for all n.

Passing to the limit and using that Y is perfectoid, so O⁺_Y = lim O⁺_Y/p^n (H^i(Y, O⁺_Y/ϖ^n) is almost S⁺/ϖ^n for i = 0 and almost zero for i > 0), gives the unique factorization; inverting p gives the map on O.
Uniqueness and the sheaf property make f^♦ bijective on all test objects.
acceptance: The normalization A¹ → {y² = x³} of the cuspidal cubic over Q_p induces an isomorphism of diamonds although it is not an isomorphism of rigid spaces (SW20 §10.2).
Compatibility: for X^sn → X the seminormalization of a rigid space over K ⊇ Q_p this gives DiamondsAndVStacks D6.9's statement that diamondification factors through seminormalization.
Non-example: a nontrivial finite étale cover of degree d > 1 is not a universal homeomorphism and its diamond map is not an isomorphism.

sources.match: Proves that f^♦ is an isomorphism for a universal homeomorphism of analytic pre-adic spaces over Spa Q_p by constructing the unique factorization of every perfectoid test map through the comparison of O⁺/p^n and the completeness of O⁺ on perfectoid spaces.

nodes.title: The v-sheaf X^⋄ of a scheme over F_p
nodes.statement: For a scheme X over F_p, X^⋄ is the v-sheaf on Perf obtained by applying the pre-adic diamondification of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 to the discrete adic space with charts Spa(A, A) for affine opens Spec A ⊂ X. Concretely, Spec(A)^⋄(Spa(R, R⁺)) = Hom_ring(A, R⁺) (characteristic p, so no untilt choice), and X^⋄ is glued along the open subfunctors Spec(A[1/g])^⋄ = {f(g) ∈ (R⁺)^×} ⊂ Spec(A)^⋄. The construction X ↦ X^⋄ is a functor from F_p-schemes to small v-sheaves; X^⋄ = (X^perf)^⋄; it commutes with finite limits and sends open (closed) immersions to open (closed) immersions.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
This is the 'formal' convention Spa(A, A); it differs from the analytic convention Spa(A, A⁺) with A⁺ the integral closure of F_p used by AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L1 for X◇.
A discrete ring A has the discrete topology, so every ring map A → R⁺ is continuous.
proofSteps: Use DiamondsAndVStacks:D6/pre-adic-diamondification for the discrete affine pairs (A, A) and glue along the open subfunctors attached to principal opens.
Frobenius of R⁺ is bijective, so Hom(A, R⁺) = Hom(A^perf, R⁺): X^⋄ = (X^perf)^⋄ with X^perf from SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.24.
Finite limits: Hom(A ⊗_C B, R⁺) = Hom(A, R⁺) ×_{Hom(C, R⁺)} Hom(B, R⁺) on affines, then glue.

A closed immersion Spec(A/I) → Spec A gives maps annihilating every element of I; I need not be finitely generated. After a v-cover by totally disconnected perfectoid test objects, the simultaneous vanishing locus of all these functions is closed and weakly generalizing. Apply the parent's closed-sub-v-sheaf criterion there and descend closed immersions; arbitrary intersections, rather than a finite generating set, handle general I.
acceptance: Spec(F_p)^⋄ is the final v-sheaf *, and (Spec F_p[t])^⋄ sends Spa(R, R⁺) to R⁺.

nodes.title: Quasicompact spaces over a valuation spectrum have a minimal image point
nodes.statement: Let V be a valuation ring, Z a nonempty quasicompact topological space and g : Z → Spec V a continuous map. Then the image g(Z) ⊂ Spec V has a unique minimal point for the generization order: a point of the image that is a specialization of every other point of the image (the largest prime ideal in the image).
hypotheses: Spec V is totally ordered by specialization; Z is nonempty and quasicompact. Nonemptiness is necessary and is already present in the suggested Lean signature.
proofSteps: Write V as a filtered union of valuation subrings V_i of finite rank; then Spec V = lim Spec V_i, each a finite chain.
The image of Z in Spec V_i is a nonempty subset of a finite chain, with a most special point z_i; the z_i are compatible and define z ∈ Spec V.

If z were not in g(Z), every image point would be a proper generization of z, so the preimages of the opens U_i of proper generizations of z_i would cover Z; quasicompactness and cofilteredness give one i with preimage all of Z, contradicting z_i ∈ image.
acceptance: For V a field the image is the unique point.
For Z = Spec V and g the identity the minimal point is the closed point.

Quasicompactness is needed: for V with primes p_1 ⊊ p_2 ⊊ ⋯ whose union is the maximal ideal and Z = {p_n : n ≥ 1} with the subspace topology (not quasicompact), no image point specializes all others.
The empty space has empty image and no minimal image point, so it is excluded. For the identity of Spec V the minimal image point is its closed point.

nodes.title: Full faithfulness of X ↦ X^⋄ on perfect schemes
nodes.statement: The functor X ↦ X^⋄ of D7/perfect-scheme-v-sheaf from perfect schemes of characteristic p to small v-sheaves on Perf is fully faithful: for perfect schemes X and Y, Hom(Y, X) → Hom(Y^⋄, X^⋄) is bijective.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
No finiteness or separatedness hypotheses on X or Y.
proofSteps: Affine target X = Spec R: both sides turn colimits in Y into limits, so take Y = Spec S; the v-cover Spa(S((t^{1/p^∞})), S[[t^{1/p^∞}]]) of Y^⋄ embeds Hom(Y^⋄, X^⋄) into Hom(R, S[[t^{1/p^∞}]]), and equality of the two pullbacks to the self-product forces the image to lie in S, checked after mapping S to fields.
Faithfulness in general: two maps with the same ⋄ agree on underlying spaces, by surjectivity of |Y^⋄| → |Y| (DiamondsAndVStacks D6.8), and then agree by the affine case.

Fullness: successively for Y = Spec K (one point, factor through an affine open), Y = Spec V a valuation ring (the key case, using D7/minimal-point-lemma to show the map factors through U^⋄ for an affine U), Y = Spec ∏V_i (Stone–Čech compactification of the index set and splitting of open covers), and general Y by v-descent of perfect schemes.
v-descent: Hom(−, X) is a v-sheaf on perfect schemes, so a map of v-sheaves defined on a v-cover by products of valuation rings descends.
acceptance: For X = Spec F_p[t^{1/p^∞}], the endomorphisms of the v-sheaf X^⋄ are exactly the ring endomorphisms of F_p[t^{1/p^∞}].
Non-example for non-perfect schemes: Spec F_p[t] and its perfection have isomorphic ⋄, but are not isomorphic.
Compatibility: Gleason's Theorem 2.32 (D7/discrete-source-full-faithfulness) specializes to this statement when the target is a perfect scheme.

nodes.title: The olivine spectrum Spo(B, B⁺) of a Huber pair
nodes.statement: For a Huber pair (B, B⁺), Spo(B, B⁺) is the set of pairs x = (|·|^h_x, |·|^a_x) of points of Spa(B, B⁺) such that |·|^a_x has rank at most 1 and is a vertical generization of |·|^h_x, with the topology generated by the classical localizations U_{b₁≤b₂≠0} = {|b₁|^h ≤ |b₂|^h ≠ 0} and the analytic localizations N_{b₁≪b₂} = {|b₁|^a < |b₂|^a ≠ 0}. The first projection h : Spo(B, B⁺) → Spa(B, B⁺) is continuous, surjective and functorial. A point is discrete if |·|^a is trivial, d-analytic otherwise (analytic if h(x) is analytic, meromorphic otherwise), bounded if |B|^a ≤ 1, and formal if bounded and d-analytic; supp(x) = supp h(x), the specialization ideal sp(x) = {b ∈ B⁺ : |b|^h < 1} and, for bounded x, the deformation ideal def(x) = {b ∈ B : |b|^a < 1}.
hypotheses: (B, B⁺) is a Huber pair, not necessarily complete or over Z_p; Spa(B, B⁺) is Tau Ceti's TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.spa.
proofSteps: Each fibre h^{-1}(h(x)) has at most one d-analytic and at most one discrete point, two exactly when h(x) is discrete and microbial.
Classical and analytic localizations are functorial in (B, B⁺), so Spo is a functor and h is continuous.
acceptance: Spo(B, B⁺) has more points than Spa(B, B⁺) exactly over the discrete microbial points.
Algebraic points (|·|^h trivial) correspond to the prime ideals of B/B°° that are open.

nodes.title: The olivine spectrum computes |Spd(B, B⁺)|
nodes.statement: For a complete Huber pair (B, B⁺) over Z_p, sending a point Spa(C, C⁺) → Spa(B, B⁺) of Spd(B, B⁺) to the images of the closed point and of the rank-one point defines a continuous bijection π : |Spd(B, B⁺)| → Spo(B, B⁺), functorial in (B, B⁺) and compatible with the generization patterns. It is a homeomorphism when (B, B) is a formal Huber pair, when (B, B⁺) is Tate, and when (B, B⁺) is topologically of finite type over a formal Huber pair (B₀, B₀) with B⁺ the integral closure of the image of the rings of integral elements; on the bounded locus it is always a homeomorphism.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
Huber pairs over Z_p; complete.
proofSteps: Continuity: analytic localizations pull back to open loci on perfectoid tests; classical localizations pull back to open valuation-comparison loci, locally unions of rational opens.
Injectivity: two points with the same image have the same residue field data and are equivalent through a common perfectoid field over (K_{h(x)}, K⁺_{h(x)}).
Surjectivity: realize each pair (|·|^h, |·|^a) by a perfectoid field with an open bounded valuation subring.
Formal pairs: compare with the analytic pre-adic space Spa(B[[t]])_{t≠0}, a v-cover whose space equals that of its diamond, and transport opens.
Topologically finite type: induct on the number of variables using rational localizations and closed immersions, which preserve the olivine property (Gleason Propositions 2.11, 2.22).
acceptance: For (B, B⁺) = (C, O_C) a perfectoid field, π is the homeomorphism |Spd C| = |Spa C| of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.3.
For B = F_p[[u]] discrete, |Spd(B)| has four points, not the three of Spa(B).
For (Z_p, Z_p), |Spd Z_p| is the two-point Sierpiński space, matching DiamondsAndVStacks D6.8's computation.

sources.locator: Introduction, Theorem 1, p. 3; §2.2, Propositions 2.13 and 2.14, p. 14; Lemma 2.18 and Proposition 2.19, pp. 15–16; Proposition 2.22, p. 17; Proposition 2.27, p. 18
sources.match: Constructs the comparison map, proves that it is a continuous bijection with the same generization pattern, a homeomorphism for formal pairs and pairs topologically of finite type over a formal pair, and always on the bounded locus.

nodes.title: Schematic closed subsets of the olivine spectrum are zero loci of open primes
nodes.statement: Let (B, B⁺) be a Huber pair. Call Z ⊂ Spo(B, B⁺) schematic if it is a union of images Spo(m)(Spo(A, A)) along maps of Huber pairs m : (B, B⁺) → (A, A) with A discrete. For a discrete A and m: the image of Spo(A, A) is h^{-1} of the image of Spa(A), which is stable under horizontal specializations and vertical generizations. If Z is schematic and closed then Z = σ^{-1}(V(I)) for the support map σ : Spo(B, B⁺) → Spec B and some ideal I of B open for the topology of B.
hypotheses: (B, B⁺) a Huber pair; σ(x) = supp h(x).
proofSteps: A continuous map to a discrete pair has open kernel and kills every topologically nilpotent element. Pass to B/(B·B°°), with the integral closure of the image of B⁺ as its plus subring; this is a discrete Huber pair. Topologically nilpotent elements need not themselves be an ideal of B.
Images of discrete pairs are stable under the stated specializations and generizations (Gleason Proposition 2.34), hence Z = σ^{-1}(σ(Z)).
The trivial-valuation section Spec B → Spa(B, B⁺) of the support map identifies σ(Z) with the preimage of h(Z), which is closed by Proposition 2.28.
acceptance: For B = A discrete and Z = Spo(A, A) itself, I = 0.
For A discrete and m : A → A/I with I an open prime, the image of Spo(A/I, A/I) is σ^{-1}(V(I)).
For B = F_p × F_p discrete, the whole olivine spectrum is schematic and closed. Its defining radical ideal is zero, which is not prime. The empty locus is allowed by taking I = B.

sources.locator: §2.5, Proposition 2.34, p. 21; Definition 2.35 and Proposition 2.36, p. 22
sources.match: The image and support arguments show that schematic closed subsets are inverse images of V(I) for an open ideal I; the claim that I must be prime in Proposition 2.36 is false (E6).

nodes.title: v-covers of perfect affine schemes are detected by ⋄
nodes.statement: Let f : S → T be a morphism of perfect affine F_p-schemes. Then f^⋄ : S^⋄ → T^⋄ is a quasicompact map of v-sheaves, and f is universally subtrusive (a v-cover in the sense of Bhatt–Scholze and Rydh) if and only if f^⋄ is a surjection of v-sheaves. A small family (S_i → T) is a v-cover if and only if ⨿ S_i^⋄ → T^⋄ is surjective. Equivalently, Spec B → Spec A is universally subtrusive iff |Spa(B)| → |Spa(A)| (discrete pairs) is surjective.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
Perfect affine schemes; a family is a v-cover when a finite subfamily is.
proofSteps: Quasicompactness: for perfect discrete A, the bounded locus of Spd(A) is everything, and maps of bounded loci along adic maps are representable in spatial diamonds (Gleason Lemma 2.26).
For quasicompact maps surjectivity of v-sheaves is surjectivity on underlying spaces (DiamondsAndVStacks D4).
Through D7/olivine-comparison, surjectivity of |Spd(B)| → |Spd(A)| is surjectivity of Spo(B, B) → Spo(A, A), which is surjectivity of Spa(B) → Spa(A) by Proposition 2.34.
The adic-spectrum criterion for universal subtrusiveness is ArcTopologyAndDescent AT.1/v-cover-geometry.
acceptance: The identity of a perfect affine scheme is a v-cover and its ⋄ is surjective.
A proper surjection of perfect schemes, such as the perfected blow-up of the origin in the perfect affine plane, is a v-cover.
Non-example: the inclusion of the generic point Spec F_p(t)^perf → Spec F_p[t]^perf is not a v-cover, and its ⋄ misses the points of the closed points.

sources.match: Recalls universal subtrusiveness, its adic-spectrum criterion, proves that f^⋄ is quasicompact and that f is a v-cover exactly when f^⋄ is surjective, for single maps and for families.

nodes.title: Maps from perfect discrete adic spaces to pre-adic spaces
nodes.statement: Let Y be a perfect discrete adic space over F_p (locally Spa(A, A⁺) with A perfect and discrete) and X a pre-adic space over Z_p. Then Hom(Y, X) → Hom(Y^♢, X^♢) is bijective. In particular ♢ is fully faithful on perfect discrete adic spaces over F_p, and every map Spd(A, A⁺) → Spd(B, B⁺) to a complete Huber pair over Z_p comes from a unique map of Huber pairs (B, B⁺) → (A, A⁺).
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
A⁺ ⊂ A is a ring of integral elements; A carries the discrete topology.
proofSteps: Every map Spd(A, A⁺) → Spd(Z_p) factors through Spd F_p (Gleason Lemma 2.30).

Affine target: test against Spa(A((t^{1/p^∞})), A⁺ + t^{1/p^∞}A[[t^{1/p^∞}]]), which covers the bounded locus; invariance under automorphisms of the test object and topological nilpotence of t^{p^n}f*(b) force f*(b) ∈ A, giving a ring map (B, B⁺) → (A, A⁺); agreement off the bounded locus uses ultraproducts of geometric points (Lemma 2.31).

General X: show that a map g : Y^♢ → X^♢ descends to a continuous |Y| → |X| through the olivine spectrum; reduce to Y = Spa(A, A⁺) with A⁺ ⊂ A valuation rings with the same fraction field, where an exotic map would contradict quasicompactness via D7/minimal-point-lemma (Lemma 2.33).
Glue the affine factorizations.
acceptance: For Y = Spec(S) with S perfect and X = Spec(R) perfect this recovers D7/perfect-scheme-full-faithfulness on affines.
For Y = Spa(F_p) and X = Spa(Z_p, Z_p) both sides are a single point.
Perfection of the source is needed: for the non-perfect discrete Y = Spa(F_p[t], F_p[t]) the endomorphism of Y^♢ = (Y^perf)^♢ induced by t ↦ t^{1/p} is not induced by an endomorphism of Y.

nodes.title: Small scheme-theoretic v-sheaves
nodes.statement: For a cutoff cardinal κ let PCAlg^op_κ be the category of perfect affine F_p-schemes whose underlying space and ring of global sections have cardinality at most κ, with the v-topology (a small family is a cover when a finite subfamily is universally subtrusive), and SchPerf~_κ its topos. For κ < λ the inverse-image (extension) functor induced by inclusion of sites gives fully faithful embeddings SchPerf~_κ → SchPerf~_λ; the category SchPerf~ of small scheme-theoretic v-sheaves is the filtered union over all cutoff cardinals. Representable functors of perfect schemes are objects; the topology is subcanonical.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).

Scheme-theoretic v-sheaves are sheaves on the category PCAlg^op of perfect affine F_p-schemes with the v-topology of ArcTopologyAndDescent AT.1, made small through cutoff cardinals as in DiamondsAndVStacks D0/D2.
proofSteps: Every morphism from a perfect affine scheme to a κ-small one factors through a κ-small v-cover (Gleason Lemma 3.10), so v-covers are filtered colimits of κ-small v-covers.

Hence the inverse-image extension from the κ-small to the λ-small topos is fully faithful (Gleason Proposition 3.9), and the colimit over cutoff cardinals exists as in DiamondsAndVStacks D0/cutoff-cardinal.
Subcanonicity is ArcTopologyAndDescent AT.1/perfection-v-comparison.
acceptance: A perfect scheme represents an object of SchPerf~.

nodes.title: Reduction of Spd(A, A⁺) and of pre-adic spaces
nodes.statement: Let X be a pre-adic space over Z_p and X^na → X the reduced non-analytic adic space of its non-analytic locus (locally Spa(A/(A·A°°), integralClosure(image(A⁺ → A/(A·A°°))))). For a Huber pair (A, A⁺) over Z_p, Spd(A, A⁺)^red is represented by Spec(A_red) with A_red = (A/A·A°°)^perf; in particular Spd(A)^red = Spec((A/I)^perf) for a formal Huber pair with ideal of definition I, and Spd(Z_p)^red = Spec F_p.

nodes.title: Formal adicness detects adicness for formal Huber pairs
nodes.statement: For formal Huber pairs (A, A) and (B, B) over Z_p with ideals of definition I_A, I_B and a continuous map B → A, Spa(A) → Spa(B) is adic (some I_A^m ⊂ A·I_B) if and only if Spd(A) → Spd(B) is formally adic. For a Huber pair (A, A⁺) with a map to Spa(Z_p), if Spd(A, A⁺) → Spd Z_p is formally adic then Spa(A, A⁺) → Spa(Z_p) is adic.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
proofSteps: The reduction square involves Spec(A_red) and (Spec(A/I_B A)^perf); adicness makes them agree after perfection.
Conversely, formal adicness identifies the Zariski closed subsets of I_A and I_B·A in Spec A, so I_A is nil modulo I_B·A and, being finitely generated, I_A^m ⊂ I_B·A.

For (A, A⁺): the analytic locus U^♢ → Spd(A, A⁺) is formally adic (D8/quasiseparated-diamonds-have-empty-reduction, D8/reduction-of-huber-pairs); composing, formal adicness forces the analytic locus to lie over Spd Q_p.
acceptance: Z_p[[T]] with the (p, T)-adic topology over Z_p with the p-adic topology: not adic and not formally adic.
Z_p⟨T⟩ over Z_p: adic and formally adic.

sources.match: Proves that a map of formal Huber pairs is adic exactly when its Spd is formally adic, and that formal p-adicness of Spd(A, A⁺) forces adicness over Z_p.

nodes.title: Spd Z_p is formally separated and formally p-adic sheaves have formally adic diagonal
nodes.statement: Spd Z_p is formally separated. If F is formally p-adic then the diagonal F → F × F is formally adic.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. proofSteps: The diagonal of Spd Z_p pulls back along Spa(R, R⁺) → Spd Z_p × Spd Z_p to the locus where two untilts agree, the intersection of two closed Cartier divisors of Spa W(R⁺) minus V([ϖ]), a Zariski closed subset represented by a perfectoid space.

For F formally p-adic: F ×_{Spd Z_p} F → Spd Z_p is formally adic, the relative diagonal is formally adic by Cartesian-square generalities, and F ×_{Spd Z_p} F → F × F is a base change of the diagonal of Spd Z_p.

nodes.title: Injectivity of the reduction counit and the formally-adic criterion
nodes.statement: For a small v-sheaf F the diagonal F → F × F is formally adic iff the counit (F^red)^⋄ → F is injective; in that case a section m ∈ F(A, A⁺) lies in (F^red)^⋄ iff v-locally on Spa(A, A⁺) it extends along Spa(R, R⁺) → Spec(R⁺)^⋄ to a map Spec(R⁺)^⋄ → F. If (G^red)^⋄ → G is injective and F ×_G (G^red)^⋄ is represented by a reduced scheme-theoretic v-sheaf, then any f : F → G is formally adic.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
proofSteps: A map of sheaves is injective iff its diagonal square is Cartesian; (F^red)^⋄ is the sheafification of (R, R⁺) ↦ Hom(Spec(R⁺)^⋄, F).
For the criterion: with T reduced and T^⋄ = F ×_G (G^red)^⋄, compute (T^⋄)^red = F^red ×_{G^red} ((G^red)^⋄)^red = F^red using the triangle identities, so (F^red)^⋄ = T^⋄.
acceptance: Spd(A) for a formal Huber pair satisfies the criterion with (Spd A^red)^⋄ = Spec(A_red)^⋄.

sources.match: Characterizes formal adicness of the diagonal by injectivity of the counit, describes sections of (F^red)^⋄, and gives a criterion for formal adicness through a reduced fibre.

nodes.title: Formally closed subsheaves of Spd(A) have reduction Spec(A/J)
nodes.statement: Let (A, A) be a formal Huber pair over Z_p and F → Spd(A) a formally closed immersion. Then (F^red)^⋄ = Spec(A/J)^⋄ for some open ideal J ⊂ A; in particular F^red is represented by the perfection of a closed subscheme of Spec(A_red).
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
proofSteps: Pull back F → Spd(A) to a v-cover by totally disconnected perfectoid spaces. On each such space the parent classifies closed sub-v-sheaves by weakly generalizing closed subsets. Descent for closed immersions and for subobjects gives the corresponding closed subset |F| in Spo(A,A); this does not assume that Spd(A) itself is totally disconnected.
By formal adicness |(F^red)^⋄| = |F| ∩ |Spec(A_red)^⋄|, and by D8/adjunction-injectivity-criterion it is a schematic closed subset of Spo(A, A).
D7/schematic-closed-subsets identifies it with V(J) for an open ideal J.
acceptance: For F = Spd(A/J) with J open (A/J discrete), F^red = Spec((A/J)^perf), which depends only on the radical of J.

nodes.title: The specialization map of a Tate Huber pair
nodes.statement: For a Tate Huber pair (A, A⁺) over Z_p, sp_A : |Spa(A, A⁺)| → |Spec(A⁺_red)| sends x to the prime {a ∈ A⁺ : |a(x)| < 1} of A⁺, which contains A⁺°° and so is a point of Spec(A⁺/A⁺°°) = Spec(A⁺_red) (the perfection does not change the space). It is functorial in maps of Tate Huber pairs, continuous, surjective, spectral and closed; for a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid Spa(R, R⁺) it is a homeomorphism.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
A⁺_red = (A⁺/A⁺·A⁺°°)^perf; for perfectoid pairs A⁺°° is the radical of a pseudouniformizer.
proofSteps: The set {a ∈ A⁺ : |a(x)| < 1} is a prime ideal since |·(x)| is multiplicative and ≤ 1 on A⁺; it contains the topologically nilpotent elements.
Continuity, surjectivity, spectrality and closedness: Bhatt's notes Theorem 8.1.2 (cited by Gleason Proposition 4.2), through the description of Spa(A, A⁺) as an inverse limit over formal models.

Strictly totally disconnected case: points with the same image lie in the same connected component; components are Spa(C, C⁺) (DiamondsAndVStacks D1/strictly-totally-disconnected), where sp is the bijection between points of Spa(C, C⁺) and primes of C⁺ above m_C (valuation rings between C⁺ and O_C).
acceptance: For (C, O_C) a perfectoid field sp_C maps the unique point to the closed point of Spec(k_C).

nodes.title: Formalizations and v-formalizing v-sheaves
nodes.statement: Let F be a small v-sheaf, (A, A⁺) a Tate Huber pair and f : Spd(A, A⁺) → F. A formalization of f is a map t : Spd(A⁺) → F restricting to f, where Spd(A⁺) = Spd(A⁺, A⁺) with the ϖ-adic topology. F formalizes f if one exists, v-formalizes f if f becomes formalizable after a v-cover Spa(B, B⁺) → Spa(A, A⁺); F is formalizing if it formalizes all maps from affinoid perfectoid spaces and v-formalizing if it v-formalizes all of them. F is v-locally formal if there is a surjection ⨿_i Spd(B_i) → F from formal Huber pairs over Z_p; this is equivalent to v-formalizing, and to the existence of a surjection ⨿_j Spd(R_j⁺) → F from perfectoid pairs.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
proofSteps: Spd Z_p and Spd(B) for formal Huber pairs are formalizing: a map Spa(A, A⁺) → Spd Z_p is an untilt, given by a primitive ξ ∈ W(R⁺), which defines Spd(R⁺) → Spd Z_p (Gleason Lemma 4.7).
v-formalizing implies v-locally formal by refining a surjection from affinoid perfectoid spaces; the converse because maps into Spd(B_i) formalize.

Permanence (Gleason Proposition 4.8): images of v-formalizing sheaves under surjections are v-formalizing; S^⋄ is formalizing for perfect affine S and v-formalizing for any scheme-theoretic v-sheaf; nonempty v-formalizing sheaves have nonempty reduction, so quasiseparated diamonds are not v-formalizing.
acceptance: Spd(O_C) is formalizing; Spd(C, O_C) is not v-formalizing.

nodes.title: Formalizations into a formally separated v-sheaf are unique
nodes.statement: If F is formally separated and f : Spa(R, R⁺) → F is a map from an affinoid perfectoid space of characteristic p, then f has at most one formalization Spd(R⁺) → F. Fibre products of v-formalizing sheaves over a formally separated sheaf are v-formalizing, and v-formalizing formally separated v-sheaves are stable under fibre products and contain Spd Z_p.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
proofSteps: Two formalizations g₁, g₂ define Spd(R⁺) → F × F; the pullback of the diagonal is a formally closed subsheaf G ⊂ Spd(R⁺) containing Spa(R, R⁺).

By D8/formally-closed-subsheaves-of-formal-pairs, G^red is a closed subscheme of Spec(R⁺_red); it contains the formal specializations of all geometric points, so by surjectivity of D9/tate-specialization-map it is everything.
Hence |G| = |Spd(R⁺)| and G = Spd(R⁺), so g₁ = g₂. The fibre-product statements follow by choosing compatible formalizations and D8/spd-zp-formally-separated.
acceptance: For F = Spd(O_C) every map from Spa(C, O_C) has the unique formalization Spd(O_C) → Spd(O_C).

sources.match: Proves uniqueness of formalizations into formally separated v-sheaves by analysing the formally closed equalizer subsheaf of Spd(R⁺), and stability of v-formalizing formally separated sheaves under fibre products.

nodes.title: The specialization map sp_F : |F| → |F^red|
nodes.statement: For a specializing v-sheaf F, sp_F : |F| → |F^red| is the unique map such that for every surjection ⨿ Spd(B_i) → F from formal Huber pairs, sp_F composed with |Spd(B_i)| → |F| equals |f^red| composed with the specialization |Spd(B_i)| → |Spec((B_i)_red)|. Concretely, represent x ∈ |F| by a formalizable Spa(K, K⁺) → F, take its unique formalization Spd(K⁺) → F, apply (−)^red to get Spec((K⁺)_red) → F^red, and take the image of the closed point. sp_F is continuous and functorial in maps of specializing v-sheaves.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
proofSteps: Well defined and independent of choices by D9/unique-formalization (Gleason Remark 4.13).

Continuity: in the square with a cover ⨿ Spd(R_i⁺) → F, the left map is a quotient map, f^red is continuous (D8/scheme-theoretic-underlying-space) and the sp_{R_i⁺} are continuous (D9/tate-specialization-map).
acceptance: For F = Spd(O_C), sp_F maps both points to the point of Spec k_C.

nodes.title: Formal schemes give prekimberlites
nodes.statement: Let 𝔛 be a separated locally noetherian formal scheme over Spf Z_p (so p lies in an ideal of definition locally) and 𝔛^ad = t(𝔛) its adic space (AdicSpacesPartII R2). Then 𝔛^♢ := (𝔛^ad)^♢ is a prekimberlite with (𝔛^♢)^red = (𝔛_red)^perf, its counit is the closed immersion ((𝔛_red)^perf)^⋄ → 𝔛^♢ of the non-analytic locus, and (𝔛^♢)^an = (𝔛^ad_a)^♢ is the diamond of the analytic locus.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
Formal schemes are those of AdicSpacesPartII F0 (locally noetherian, with the fully faithful functor t to adic spaces); separated means 𝔛_red is separated.
proofSteps: v-locally formal: 𝔛^♢ is covered by the Spd(A) of affine opens Spf A.

Reduction: D8/reduction-of-huber-pairs gives (𝔛^♢)^red = (𝔛^na,♢)^red = (𝔛_red)^perf; the counit is the map of the non-analytic locus, a closed immersion (Gleason Proposition 1.21(6); DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 diamond_formal_complement).

Separatedness over Spd Z_p: quasiseparatedness from quasicompactness of affine intersections and representability of the diagonal; the valuative criterion (DiamondsAndVStacks D3) reduces to separatedness of 𝔛_red via maps Spf(K⁺) → 𝔛 as pairs of a map from Spf(O_K) and a map from Spec(K⁺/K°°).

The closed counit already established is a monomorphism. Apply D8/adjunction-injectivity-criterion to obtain formal adicness of the diagonal, and combine it with separatedness proved above. This proves formal separatedness without assuming that the structure map to Spd Z_p is formally p-adic.
acceptance: For 𝔛 = Spf Z_p⟨T⟩ the prekimberlite is Spd(Z_p⟨T⟩) with reduction the perfect affine line.
For 𝔛 = Spf Z_p[[T]] ((p, T)-adic) the analytic locus contains points with p = 0 and T ≠ 0, so (𝔛^♢)^an ≠ (𝔛^♢)_η.

nodes.title: Formal neighbourhoods of locally closed subsets of the reduction
nodes.statement: Let F be a prekimberlite and S ⊂ |F^red| a locally closed subset with its reduced perfect subscheme structure. Write underline(T) for the v-sheaf U ↦ Cont(|U|,T), as in Gleason §1.1. The formal neighbourhood is the sheaf pullback F̂_{/S} = F ×_{underline(|F^red|)} underline(S), using the natural specialization morphism to this topological sheaf. This condition concerns the entire image of each perfectoid test space; it does not identify |F̂_{/S}| with sp_F^{-1}(S) on individual points. For a map of prekimberlites G → F and T = S ×_{F^red} G^red, F̂_{/S} ×_F G = Ĝ_{/T}; F̂_{/S} is a prekimberlite with reduction S. It is open when S is open. For a formal pair (A,A), with ideal of definition I and finitely generated J ⊃ I, it is Spd(Â_J) over V(J), where Â_J is the J-adic completion.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
proofSteps: The pullback is taken in v-sheaves, with the topological factors underlined; a section lies in it precisely when its continuous specialization map on the entire test space lands in S. Rank-higher-than-one generizations explain why this is stronger than membership of one point in sp_F^{-1}(S).
Base change: |T| = |S| ×_{|F^red|} |G^red| and naturality of sp (Gleason Proposition 4.20).

Prekimberlite: formal separatedness is inherited by subsheaves; v-formalizing because formalizations specialize into S; the closed immersion S^⋄ → F̂_{/S} is checked for S closed (proper inclusion) and S open, then composed (Proposition 4.21).
Completion: maps A → R⁺ whose reduction lands in V(J) send J into a topologically nilpotent ideal, hence are J-adically continuous and extend to B (Proposition 4.19).
acceptance: For S = |F^red| the formal neighbourhood is F.

nodes.title: Constructible formal neighbourhoods are open
nodes.statement: If F is a prekimberlite and S ⊂ |F^red| is locally closed and constructible, then F̂_{/S} → F is an open immersion. For S closed with ideal (i₁, …, i_n) locally, and a formalized test map Spd(R⁺) → F with lifts j_k ∈ R⁺, the base change is the open locus where all j_k are topologically nilpotent. It is formally adic only when S is open.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
proofSteps: The question is Zariski local on F^red; reduce to S closed constructible in Spec A, defined by a finitely generated ideal.

Over a formalized test object, D9/formal-neighbourhood (completion case) and the analytic-localization description of the olivine spectrum (Gleason Lemma 2.24) identify the base change with ⋂ N_{j_k≪1}, an open subsheaf.
Openness descends along v-covers (DiamondsAndVStacks D3/v-local-nature-of-morphism-classes).
acceptance: For S the origin of the perfect affine line over F_p, Spd(F_p[[T]]) → Spd(F_p[T]) is an open immersion that is not formally adic.

nodes.title: Heuer's v-sheaf X^{⋄/◦} of a perfect scheme
nodes.statement: For a scheme X over F_p, X^{⋄/◦} is the analytic sheafification of (R, R⁺) ↦ X(Spec(R⁺/R°°)) on affinoid perfectoid spaces; for affine X no sheafification is needed. It is a v-sheaf commuting with finite limits and open immersions, with a natural map X^⋄ → X^{⋄/◦}. For X perfect, (X^{⋄/◦})^red = X, and X^{⋄/◦}(Spa(R, R⁺)) = X^{⋄/◦}(Spd(R⁺)) for totally disconnected Spa(R, R⁺): maps from totally disconnected spaces formalize uniquely.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
proofSteps: v-sheaf property: Heuer's Lemma 5.2 (cited by Gleason Definition 4.23).
Reduction: X ⊂ (X^{⋄/◦})^red is formal; for the converse test against Spd(R((t^{1/p^∞})), R[[t^{1/p^∞}]]) where Heuer's lemma computes the values as maps A → R (Gleason Proposition 4.24).

nodes.title: Étale maps of perfect schemes give formally adic étale maps of Heuer sheaves
nodes.statement: For a quasicompact separated étale map V → X of perfect F_p-schemes, V^{⋄/◦} → X^{⋄/◦} is separated, quasicompact, formally adic and étale. On affine tests Spa(R,R⁺), use the unique completed formally étale lift of the prescribed étale algebra over the reduced integral ring. Its generic fibre, with the canonical integral subring, represents the pullback; work on affine étale charts and glue. Uniqueness is in the category of complete formal lifts, not among all ordinary étale R⁺-algebras.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
proofSteps: X ↦ X^{⋄/◦} commutes with finite limits and open immersions; separatedness from the open-and-closed diagonal.

For formal adicness, compare V^⋄ with V^{⋄/◦} ×_{X^{⋄/◦}} X^⋄ on formalized tests. Étale-site invariance under perfection and nil ideals identifies the reduction data, and completed henselian lifting gives the formally étale lift over R⁺; here R⁺ can be nonnoetherian.

On affine étale charts, take the completed lift, invert a pseudo-uniformizer, and use its canonical integral subring to obtain the étale adic pullback. Glue the charts. Finite presentation and the quasicompact separated hypothesis give quasicompactness and separatedness.
acceptance: For V → X an open immersion, V^{⋄/◦} → X^{⋄/◦} is an open immersion.

For the identity residue algebra, R⁺ and R⁺ × R⁺[1/ϖ] are distinct ordinary étale lifts with the same reduction. Completion removes the second factor, so uniqueness must be formulated for completed lifts.

sources.match: Proves the four geometric properties using étale lifting; the affine lifting step is used in its completed formal sense (E7), with the nonnoetherian lifting prerequisite requested from SF.0.

nodes.title: Reduction is an equivalence on étale formal neighbourhoods
nodes.statement: For a prekimberlite F, the reduction functor gives an equivalence between (F)_{qc,for-ét} and the category of quasicompact separated étale perfect schemes over F^red, restricting to an equivalence between injective objects (open formal neighbourhoods) and quasicompact open immersions; F̂_{/V} is a quasi-inverse. If F = 𝔛^♢ for a formal scheme 𝔛, every étale formal neighbourhood is 𝔜^♢ for a formal scheme 𝔜.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
proofSteps: A morphism inducing an isomorphism on reductions is an isomorphism: the image is an open subsheaf containing (F^red)^⋄, hence everything, and injectivity is checked on geometric points Spa(C, C⁺) ⊂ Spd(C⁺) by counting components (Gleason Theorem 4.27, Step 1).
Full faithfulness: maps over F correspond to open and closed subsheaves of the fibre product projecting isomorphically, and likewise for reductions (Step 2).
Essential surjectivity: D9/etale-formal-neighbourhood (Step 3).
Formal schemes: the étale site of a formal scheme is that of its reduction (AdicSpacesPartII R2/formal-etale-site-invariance).
acceptance: For F = Spd Z_p, étale formal neighbourhoods correspond to finite products of finite fields over F_p, i.e. to Spd of finite products of unramified extensions W(F_q).

nodes.title: The two v-sheaves X^♢ and X^⋄ of an O-scheme
nodes.statement: Let O be a complete discrete valuation ring flat over Z_p with perfect residue field. For an O-algebra A, Spec(A)^♢ sends Spa(R, R⁺) to marked untilts R^♯ over O with an O-algebra map A → R^♯, and Spec(A)^⋄ to those with a map A → R^{♯+}. Both glue along localizations ({|g| ≠ 0}, resp. {|g| = 1}) to functors X ↦ X^♢, X^⋄ from O-schemes to v-sheaves over Spd O. For X locally of finite type, X^⋄ = (X̂)^♢ for the π-adic completion X̂ (a formal scheme) and X^♢ = (X^an)^♢ for Huber's analytification over Spa O. There is a natural map X^⋄ → X^♢: a monomorphism for X separated, an open immersion for X separated of finite type, an isomorphism for X proper.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
O = O_E as in the D10 conventions; X^♢ is the analytic convention of AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L1/mixed-characteristic-scheme-diamond, X^⋄ the formal one.
proofSteps: Gluing: localization A → A[1/g] gives the open loci where g is a unit of R^♯, resp. of R^{♯+}.

Two-step description: the forgetful functor from discrete adic spaces over Spa O_disc to O-schemes has adjoints Spec A ↦ Spa(A, A) and Spa(A, Õ) (Õ the integral closure of O in A); base change along O_disc → O and Huber's relative analytification over Spa(O,O), requested as an extension of R1's field-base construction, gives X̂ and X^an (AGLR Lemma 2.11).
Monomorphism: Spec A ⊂ Spec A⁺ is schematically dense, so maps agreeing on R^♯ agree on R^{♯+} (Stacks 01RH).
Open immersion for finite type: check for affine space by hand and pull back along a closed immersion into it.
Isomorphism for proper X: surjective on points by the valuative criterion of properness.
acceptance: For X = Spec O, X^⋄ = X^♢ = Spd O.

nodes.title: Generic fibres of formal schemes locally formally of finite type
nodes.statement: For 𝔛 locally formally of finite type over Spf O_E, the Huber generic fibre 𝔛^ad_η = 𝔛^ad ×_{Spa O_E} Spa(E, O_E) is the adic space r(𝔛^rig) of Berthelot's generic fibre (Conrad's 𝔛^rig), compatibly with maps, open immersions and the specialization maps; and 𝔛^♢ ×_{Spd O_E} Spd E = (𝔛^ad_η)^♢ = r(𝔛^rig)^♢, a locally spatial diamond.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).

E/Q_p is a complete discretely valued field with ring of integers O_E, uniformizer π and perfect residue field k; a formal scheme locally formally of finite type over Spf O_E is an object of Conrad's category FS_{O_E} (AdicSpacesPartII R2/berthelot-type-rig-functor-nonnoetherian-base): locally noetherian, with a continuous structure map to Spf O_E and 𝔛_red locally of finite type over k; affine charts are quotients of O_E[[q_1,…,q_n]]⟨T_1,…,T_m⟩ with the (π,q_1,…,q_n)-adic topology. The structure map need not be adic.
proofSteps: On affine charts Spf A, 𝔛^ad_η(R, R⁺) for complete affinoid (E, O_E)-algebras is the sheafification of colim over open bounded R₀ ⊂ R⁺ of 𝔛(R₀) (Scholze–Weinstein 2013 Proposition 2.2.2), which is the functor represented by Berthelot's 𝔛^rig (de Jong Proposition 7.1.7, Conrad Theorem 3.1.5 as recorded in AdicSpacesPartII).
Both constructions glue along open formal subschemes, giving the identification and its naturality.
♢ commutes with fibre products of pre-adic spaces (Gleason Proposition 1.21(4)); the diamond of an analytic adic space is locally spatial (DiamondsAndVStacks D6.5).
acceptance: For 𝔛 = Spf O_E[[q]] the generic fibre is the open unit disc over E, and 𝔛^♢_η its diamond.
For 𝔛 = Spf O_E⟨T⟩ the generic fibre is the closed unit disc.
Non-example: the analytic locus of Spa(O_E[[q]]) is strictly larger than the generic fibre (it contains points with π = 0, q ≠ 0); the comparison is with 𝔛^ad_η, not with 𝔛^ad_a.

The universal property of Berthelot's generic fibre for formal schemes in FS_O: maps from an affinoid to 𝔛^rig are maps from models.
Uses Y_η = Y ×_{Spd O_E} Spd E and identifies it with the diamond of the rigid generic fibre.

nodes.title: Generic fibres of normal formal schemes are normal
nodes.statement: If 𝔛 is locally formally of finite type over Spf O_E and (formally) normal, i.e. covered by Spf A with A normal, then its Berthelot generic fibre 𝔛^rig is a normal rigid space; in particular it is seminormal, so DiamondsAndVStacks D6.9 applies to it.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).

E/Q_p is a complete discretely valued field with ring of integers O_E, uniformizer π and perfect residue field k; a formal scheme locally formally of finite type over Spf O_E is an object of Conrad's category FS_{O_E} (AdicSpacesPartII R2/berthelot-type-rig-functor-nonnoetherian-base): locally noetherian, with a continuous structure map to Spf O_E and 𝔛_red locally of finite type over k; affine charts are quotients of O_E[[q_1,…,q_n]]⟨T_1,…,T_m⟩ with the (π,q_1,…,q_n)-adic topology. proofSteps: The rings A are excellent, so normality of A is normality of all complete local rings; the affinoid algebras of 𝔛^rig are built from A by Berthelot's construction and inherit normality (de Jong Lemma 7.1.9, Proposition 7.2.4(c)).
Normal rings are seminormal (square–cube criterion), and normality of affinoid algebras gives seminormality of the rigid space.
acceptance: For 𝔛 = Spf O_E[[q]], 𝔛^rig is the open disc, normal.
Non-example: the formal completion of the cusp y² = x³ over O_E is not normal, and its generic fibre is not seminormal.

nodes.title: de Jong's theorem: functions on a normal formal scheme are the power-bounded functions on its generic fibre
nodes.statement: Let 𝔛 be a flat and (formally) normal formal scheme locally formally of finite type over Spf O_E. Then restriction Γ(𝔛, O_𝔛) → Γ(𝔛^rig, O°) to power-bounded (equivalently, locally power-bounded) rigid functions on the generic fibre is an isomorphism of rings.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).

E/Q_p is a complete discretely valued field with ring of integers O_E, uniformizer π and perfect residue field k; a formal scheme locally formally of finite type over Spf O_E is an object of Conrad's category FS_{O_E} (AdicSpacesPartII R2/berthelot-type-rig-functor-nonnoetherian-base): locally noetherian, with a continuous structure map to Spf O_E and 𝔛_red locally of finite type over k; affine charts are quotients of O_E[[q_1,…,q_n]]⟨T_1,…,T_m⟩ with the (π,q_1,…,q_n)-adic topology. The structure map need not be adic.
Flatness over O_E is necessary: the generic fibre of a π-torsion formal scheme forgets the torsion.
proofSteps: de Jong's proof: on Spf A, a power-bounded f restricts on each Berthelot affinoid Sp(C_n) to an element integral over the corresponding model; at each maximal ideal of A the completion is normal and the local result on Spf(Â_m) (7.3.6) puts f in A_m-completions; faithful flatness gives f in each B_n, and passing to the limit gives f ∈ A.

Lourenço's alternative: extend a locally power-bounded function from the generic fibre to the analytic locus by the First Riemann Hebbarkeitssatz for normal pseudorigid spaces, then to the whole formal scheme by his Proposition 6.2 (normal excellent nowhere discrete formal schemes: O(𝔛) = O⁺(𝔛_a)), proved with normalized blow-ups, Zariski's main theorem and the theorem on formal functions.
acceptance: For 𝔛 = Spf O_E[[q]], the bounded functions on the open unit disc are O_E[[q]].
For 𝔛 = Spf O_E⟨T⟩ the power-bounded functions on the closed disc are O_E⟨T⟩.

nodes.title: The specialization map of 𝔛^♢ restricts to Berthelot's on classical points

nodes.title: Closed immersions of small v-stacks and proper monomorphisms
nodes.statement: A morphism Y → X of small v-stacks is a closed immersion if and only if it is a quasicompact monomorphism and |Y| → |X| is a closed embedding. Consequently every proper monomorphism of small v-sheaves is a closed immersion.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. nodes.title: The v-closure of a sub-v-sheaf
nodes.statement: For a small v-stack X and a sub-v-stack Y ⊂ X (a monomorphism), the v-closure Y^cl is the intersection of all closed sub-v-stacks of X containing Y; it is a small closed sub-v-stack. A subset S ⊂ |X| is weakly generalizing if for every Spa(C, C⁺) → X, |Spa(C, C⁺)| maps into S iff its closed point does; images of maps of small v-stacks are weakly generalizing; S ↦ S ×_{|X|} X is a bijection between closed weakly generalizing subsets and closed sub-v-stacks, with |S ×_{|X|} X| = S; and Y^cl = |Y|^wgc ×_{|X|} X, where |Y|^wgc is the smallest closed weakly generalizing subset containing |Y|. v-closures commute with base change along open partially proper maps.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
proofSteps: Closedness and smallness: check after base change to totally disconnected spaces (ECD Proposition 6.4) and use that subsheaves of small sheaves are small.
Images: a map Spa(C, C⁺) → X sending the closed point into the image factors after enlarging (C, C⁺) (ECD Proposition 12.7).

Bijection: for S closed weakly generalizing its preimage in a totally disconnected cover is closed and generalizing, hence an affinoid perfectoid subset; conversely closed sub-v-stacks have weakly generalizing image and equal S ×_{|X|} X by surjectivity on points (AGLR Lemma 2.7).
Formula for Y^cl: Proposition 2.8; base change: Corollary 2.9 via the valuative criterion for partially proper maps.
acceptance: If Y ⊂ X is already closed then Y^cl = Y.

nodes.title: Formal schemes are determined by their specialization triples (Lourenço)
nodes.statement: Assume k is algebraically closed. Let C_{O_E} be the category of triples (X_η, X_s, sp) with X_η a rigid space over E, X_s a perfect scheme over k and sp : |X_η|_cl → X_s(k) a map of sets on classical points. The functor 𝔛 ↦ (𝔛^rig, (𝔛_red)^perf, sp_𝔛) from flat normal formal schemes locally formally of finite type over Spf O_E to C_{O_E} is fully faithful.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).

E/Q_p is a complete discretely valued field with ring of integers O_E, uniformizer π and perfect residue field k; a formal scheme locally formally of finite type over Spf O_E is an object of Conrad's category FS_{O_E} (AdicSpacesPartII R2/berthelot-type-rig-functor-nonnoetherian-base): locally noetherian, with a continuous structure map to Spf O_E and 𝔛_red locally of finite type over k; affine charts are quotients of O_E[[q_1,…,q_n]]⟨T_1,…,T_m⟩ with the (π,q_1,…,q_n)-adic topology. The structure map need not be adic.
k is algebraically closed. Morphisms of formal schemes are continuous over Spf O_E and need not be adic.
proofSteps: Faithfulness: two maps with the same triple agree topologically (|𝔛| = |𝔛_red^perf|), reduce to affines Spf B → Spf A, and agree on A by D10/power-bounded-functions-theorem since A ⊂ O(𝔛^rig).

In the affine fullness step, pullback of bounded analytic functions and D10/power-bounded-functions-theorem give a ring homomorphism A → B. Continuity must still be proved before this defines a morphism of formal schemes.

Let I and J be finitely generated ideals of definition in A and B. For each generator a of I, specialization compatibility and the existence of generic-fibre points above every closed point of the reduction imply that its image in B vanishes at all such closed points. The reduced special fibre is locally of finite type over algebraically closed k, so the image lies in √J. Finite generation gives an N with I^N mapping into J, and then I^{Nn} maps into J^n. This proves continuity, including for (π,q)-adic topologies. The induced reduction morphism agrees with ψ_s on all k-points, hence on the reduced perfect schemes.
Globalization: the preimage under ψ_s of an affine reduction is covered by affine reductions, and the compatibility with sp identifies the corresponding generic fibres (Lourenço Corollaries 6.5–6.6).
acceptance: The triple of Spf O_E⟨T⟩ is (closed disc, A¹_k^perf, reduction of coordinates).

Normality is needed for the affine step: for A = O_E⟨X, Y⟩/(Y² − π²X), Y/π is a power-bounded function on the generic fibre outside A, so maps of generic fibres need not come from maps of formal schemes.

For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).

E/Q_p is a complete discretely valued field with ring of integers O_E, uniformizer π and perfect residue field k; a formal scheme locally formally of finite type over Spf O_E is an object of Conrad's category FS_{O_E} (AdicSpacesPartII R2/berthelot-type-rig-functor-nonnoetherian-base): locally noetherian, with a continuous structure map to Spf O_E and 𝔛_red locally of finite type over k; affine charts are quotients of O_E[[q_1,…,q_n]]⟨T_1,…,T_m⟩ with the (π,q_1,…,q_n)-adic topology. The structure map need not be adic.

Absolute weak normality is imported from SF.0 (AGLR Definition 2.12): seminormality together with the condition that for every prime ℓ, an equality ℓ^ℓ a = b^ℓ has a unique c with a = c^ℓ and b = ℓc. This is not closure under arbitrary ℓ-th roots. For F_p-algebras it is equivalent to perfectness.

(3): X^awn → Spec O_E is of finite type by excellence and the embedding into the normalization in characteristic 0; π-adic completion preserves absolute weak normality (regular maps); then (2) and Grothendieck existence.
acceptance: For normal A this recovers D10/formal-full-faithfulness in the topologically finite type case.
For A = O_E⟨x, y⟩/(y² − x³), the absolute weak normalization is the normalization O_E⟨t⟩, and (1) gives Spd(O_E⟨t⟩) ≅ Spd(A).

nodes.title: The v-sheaf of a flat Zariski closure is the v-closure of its generic fibre
nodes.statement: Let P be a proper O_E-scheme, U ⊂ P_E a closed subscheme of the generic fibre, and X ⊂ P the scheme-theoretic closure of U, a closed subscheme of P flat over O_E with generic fibre U. Then X^♢ ⊂ P^♢ is the v-closure (D10/v-closure) of U^♢ ⊂ P^♢, where U^♢ = (U^an)^♢ ⊂ (P_E^an)^♢ = P^♢ ×_{Spd O_E} Spd E.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).

E/Q_p is a complete discretely valued field with ring of integers O_E, uniformizer π and perfect residue field k; a formal scheme locally formally of finite type over Spf O_E is an object of Conrad's category FS_{O_E} (AdicSpacesPartII R2/berthelot-type-rig-functor-nonnoetherian-base): locally noetherian, with a continuous structure map to Spf O_E and 𝔛_red locally of finite type over k; affine charts are quotients of O_E[[q_1,…,q_n]]⟨T_1,…,T_m⟩ with the (π,q_1,…,q_n)-adic topology. The structure map need not be adic.
X is flat over O_E because it is the closure of its generic fibre.
proofSteps: X → P is a closed immersion of proper O_E-schemes, so X^♢ → P^♢ is a proper monomorphism, hence a closed immersion (D10/closed-immersion-criterion; for proper schemes ♢ = ⋄).
X^♢ contains U^♢, so U^cl ⊂ X^♢.
|U^♢| = |X^♢_η| is dense in |X^♢| (D10/generic-fibre-density applied to the flat formal completion X̂, using X^♢ = X̂^♢).

|U^cl| is closed and contains |U^♢|, hence contains its closure in |X^♢|, which is all of |X^♢|; two closed sub-v-sheaves of X^♢ with the same underlying space agree (D10/v-closure, bijection with weakly generalizing closed subsets).
acceptance: For U = P_E, X = P (P flat) and the statement says P^♢ is the v-closure of its generic fibre.

Non-example: for X' = X ∪ Z with Z ⊂ P_k a closed subvariety of the special fibre not contained in X, X' is not flat and X'^♢ strictly contains the v-closure of U^♢; nilpotent structure alone is invisible to ♢.
Application: for the Grassmannian P = Gr(d, Λ)_{O_E} and U = G/P_μ ⊂ Gr(d, V)_E, the v-sheaf of the Zariski closure is the v-closure of the Schubert diamond (KPZ Lemma 3.4.1).

nodes.title: Integral models and morphisms with prescribed v-sheaves are unique
nodes.statement: (1) If X and X' are proper flat normal O_E-schemes with X^♢ ≅ X'^♢ over Spd O_E, then X ≅ X' by a unique isomorphism inducing the given one. Let M^v_{𝒢,μ} be the v-closure (D10/v-closure) of the Schubert diamond Gr_{G,μ} over Spd Ĕ in the integral Beilinson–Drinfeld Grassmannian Gr_{𝒢,Spd O_E} of GeometricSatakeAndFusion GS0, for a parahoric model 𝒢 and minuscule μ with reflex field E. Then a scheme-theoretic local model M^loc_{𝒢,μ} (proper, flat, normal, with (M^loc)^♢ = M^v_{𝒢,μ}) is unique if it exists. (2) Let ρ : 𝒢 ↪ GL(Λ) be a closed immersion extending a Hodge embedding (G, μ) ↪ (GL(V), μ_d), and assume, as Scholze–Weinstein prove, that M^v_{GL(Λ),μ_d} = Gr(d, Λ)^♢. Then there is a unique morphism ρ_* : M^loc_{𝒢,μ} → Gr(d, Λ)_{O_E} of O_E-schemes whose diamond is the map M^v_{𝒢,μ} → M^v_{GL(Λ),μ_d} induced by ρ; if the Zariski closure X̄_μ of G/P_μ in Gr(d, Λ)_{O_E} is normal with reduced special fibre then X̄_μ = M^loc_{𝒢,μ} and ρ_* is a closed immersion.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).

E/Q_p is a complete discretely valued field with ring of integers O_E, uniformizer π and perfect residue field k; a formal scheme locally formally of finite type over Spf O_E is an object of Conrad's category FS_{O_E} (AdicSpacesPartII R2/berthelot-type-rig-functor-nonnoetherian-base): locally noetherian, with a continuous structure map to Spf O_E and 𝔛_red locally of finite type over k; affine charts are quotients of O_E[[q_1,…,q_n]]⟨T_1,…,T_m⟩ with the (π,q_1,…,q_n)-adic topology. The structure map need not be adic.

The integral Grassmannians, their bounded closed subfunctors and the closed immersion Gr_{𝒢} → Gr_{GL(Λ)} induced by a closed representation are those of GeometricSatakeAndFusion GS0 (Witt geometry); this node only applies the recovery theorems to them. The identification M^v_{GL(Λ),μ_d} = Gr(d, Λ)^♢ (SW20 Corollary 21.6.10) is a hypothesis here.
proofSteps: (1) is D10/proper-scheme-full-faithfulness applied to the isomorphism and its inverse.
(2) existence and uniqueness of ρ_* is D10/proper-scheme-full-faithfulness applied to the functorial map of v-sheaf local models.

For the last clause: D10/flat-closure-diamond gives (X̄_μ)^♢ = v-closure of X_μ^♢ in Gr(d, Λ)^♢; the map M^v_{𝒢,μ} → Gr_{GL(Λ)} is a closed immersion (GS0's closed immersion of integral Grassmannians, or directly as a proper monomorphism by D10/closed-immersion-criterion), and v-closures are compatible with closed immersions, so its image is the same v-closure; hence (X̄_μ)^♢ = M^v_{𝒢,μ} and (1) applies.
acceptance: For G = GL(Λ) and minuscule μ_d, M^loc = Gr(d, Λ)_{O_E} and ρ_* is the identity.

nodes.title: Valuative prekimberlites
nodes.statement: A prekimberlite F is valuative if Heuer's specialization morphism SP_F : F → (F^red)^{⋄/◦} is partially proper (it is always separated). Separated formal schemes give valuative prekimberlites; if G → F is a partially proper map of prekimberlites with F valuative then G is valuative; formal neighbourhoods and étale formal neighbourhoods of valuative prekimberlites are valuative; and for valuative F, sp_F : |F| → |F^red| is a specializing map.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
proofSteps: Formal schemes: partial properness is local on the target (ECD Proposition 18.6); for Spd(B) the valuative criterion asks that B → R^{♯,◦} with reduction landing in R^{♯,+}_red lands in R^{♯,+}, which holds as R^{♯,+} = R^{♯,◦} ×_{R^{♯,◦}_red} R^{♯,+}_red (Gleason Proposition 4.31).
Partially proper G → F: G → (F^red)^{⋄/◦} is partially proper and G → (G^red)^{⋄/◦} separated (Proposition 4.32).
Neighbourhoods: base changes (Proposition 4.34).

Specializing: given r with sp(r) = x and a specialization y of x, pick a valuation ring dominating the local ring of the closure of x at y, refine the integral subring of the residue field of a formalizable representative of r, and lift by partial properness (Proposition 4.33).
acceptance: Spd Z_p is valuative.

nodes.title: Smelted kimberlites and their specialization map
nodes.statement: A smelted kimberlite is a pair K = (F, D) with F a valuative prekimberlite and D ⊂ F^an an open subsheaf that is a quasiseparated locally spatial diamond such that D → F is partially proper. Its specialization map is sp_D : |D| → |F| → |F^red|. The cases of interest are D = F^an and, for F over Spd O_K, D = F ×_{Spd O_K} Spd(K, O_K).
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
proofSteps: F^an → F is always partially proper for a prekimberlite (Gleason Remark 4.36), so the conditions on D = F^an reduce to it being a quasiseparated locally spatial diamond.
acceptance: For F = Spd Z_p and D = Spd Q_p, sp_D maps the point to Spec F_p.

nodes.title: Formal schemes give kimberlites
nodes.statement: For a separated locally noetherian formal scheme 𝔛 over Spf Z_p, 𝔛^♢ is a kimberlite; its specialization map on |(𝔛^♢)^an| = |𝔛^ad_a| is the specialization map λ of AdicSpacesPartII R2 composed with |𝔛_red| = |(𝔛_red)^perf|.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
proofSteps: Valuative prekimberlite: D9/formal-scheme-prekimberlite and D11/valuative-prekimberlite.
(𝔛^♢)^an = (𝔛^ad_a)^♢ is a locally spatial diamond (DiamondsAndVStacks D6.5); quasiseparated since 𝔛 is separated.

Over an affine open Spf A ⊂ 𝔛 with ideal of definition (f_1, …, f_n), sp^{-1}(Spec A_red) = Spa(A, A)_a^♢ is the finite union of the rational subsets {|f_j| ≤ |f_i| ≠ 0}, hence spatial: sp is quasicompact.

For 𝔛 = Spf Z_p[[T]], the analytic locus is the union of {|p| ≤ |T| ≠ 0} and {|T| ≤ |p| ≠ 0}.

nodes.title: Tubular neighbourhoods of smelted kimberlites
nodes.statement: For a smelted kimberlite K = (F, D) and a constructible locally closed S ⊂ |F^red|, the tubular neighbourhood is D^⊚_{/S} = F̂_{/S} ×_F D; for a kimberlite G write G^⊚_{/S} = Ĝ_{/S} ×_G G^an. Then (F̂_{/S}, D^⊚_{/S}) is a smelted kimberlite, and D^⊚_{/S} is the open subdiamond of D with underlying space the interior of sp_D^{-1}(S), which is the largest generization-stable subset of sp_D^{-1}(S); it is not the whole fibre in general.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
proofSteps: F̂_{/S} is a valuative prekimberlite (D11/valuative-prekimberlite), D^⊚_{/S} → F̂_{/S} is open and partially proper by base change, and D^⊚_{/S} → D is an open immersion (D9/constructible-formal-neighbourhood-open), so D^⊚_{/S} is a quasiseparated locally spatial diamond.

Interior: D^⊚_{/S} ⊂ (sp^{-1}_D S)^int ⊂ T, T the largest generization-stable subset; conversely for x ∈ T all generizations specialize into S, so a formalizable geometric point over x factors through F̂_{/S} (D9/formal-neighbourhood).

nodes.title: Specialization maps of smelted kimberlites are spectral and closed for kimberlites
nodes.statement: For a smelted kimberlite (F, D), sp_D : |D| → |F^red| is a specializing spectral map of locally spectral spaces (continuous for the constructible topologies). For a kimberlite G, sp_{G^an} : |G^an| → |G^red| is closed.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
proofSteps: Specializing: D11/valuative-prekimberlite and partial properness of D → F.

Spectral: work on spatial opens; a formalizable cover X = Spa(A, A⁺) → D gives a commutative square with sp_X, which is patch-continuous, and with g^red : Spec(A⁺_red) → F^red, patch-continuous because F^red is a scheme (D8/reduced-scheme-theoretic-v-sheaf); g is a surjection of compact Hausdorff patch spaces, hence a quotient map.
Closed for kimberlites: a spectral specializing map of spectral spaces is closed (DiamondsAndVStacks D0/closure-of-pro-constructible), applied over affine opens using quasicompactness of sp_{G^an}.

nodes.title: Formally closed immersions and étale formal neighbourhoods preserve kimberlite structures
nodes.statement: Let f : G → F be a formally closed immersion. If F is specializing (resp. a prekimberlite, a kimberlite) so is G, and if (F, D) is a smelted kimberlite so is (G, G ∩ D). If V → F^red is quasicompact, separated and étale and (F, D) is a smelted kimberlite (resp. F a kimberlite), then (F̂_{/V}, D ×_F F̂_{/V}) is a smelted kimberlite (resp. F̂_{/V} a kimberlite).
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
proofSteps: Specializing: G is separated as a subsheaf and (G^red)^⋄ → G is injective by formal adicness; v-formalizing by the argument of D9/unique-formalization applied to G ×_F Spd(R⁺).
Prekimberlite: (G^red)^⋄ → G is a closed immersion and (G^red)^⋄ → (F^red)^⋄ formally closed, so G^red is a closed subscheme (D8/formally-closed-subsheaves-of-formal-pairs).
Smelted and kimberlite: closed immersions are partially proper and quasicompact; G ∩ D is a quasiseparated locally spatial diamond (ECD Proposition 11.20).
Étale case: D9/etale-thickening-lemma, D11/valuative-prekimberlite and ECD Corollary 11.28.
acceptance: The special fibre (F^red)^⋄ → F of a kimberlite is a formally closed immersion and is a kimberlite with empty analytic locus.

nodes.title: Constructibly Jacobson diamonds
nodes.statement: A locally spatial diamond X is constructibly Jacobson (a cJ-diamond) if its rank-one points are dense in |X| for the constructible topology. Surjective images of cJ-diamonds, open subdiamonds of cJ-diamonds, quotients of cJ-diamonds by quasi-pro-étale J-torsors (J profinite) and étale maps to cJ-diamonds have the property; diamonds of adic spaces topologically of finite type over a complete nonarchimedean field K over Z_p are cJ, since Max(A) ⊂ Spa(A, A°) is patch-dense for A topologically of finite type over K (Huber); perfectoid unit balls are cJ.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
proofSteps: Permanence (Gleason Proposition 4.46): maps of locally spatial diamonds are spectral and generalizing; open immersions preserve patch-opens; étale maps are locally open immersions composed with finite étale maps (ECD Lemma 11.31), reduced to Galois covers, i.e. to torsors under finite groups, for which f is patch-open because the patch topology commutes with limits and f^{-1}(f(U)) = J·U.
Huber's theorem gives patch density of classical points, which are rank one (Gleason Theorem 4.47, Corollary 4.48).
acceptance: Spd(C, O_C) is a cJ-diamond (one rank-one point).

sources.locator: §4.6, Definition 4.44, Proposition 4.46, Theorem 4.47, Corollary 4.48 and Example 4.49, pp. 36–37
sources.match: Defines cJ-diamonds, proves their permanence under surjections, open immersions, profinite torsor quotients and étale maps, and that diamonds of adic spaces topologically of finite type over a field and perfectoid balls are cJ, via Huber's density theorem.

nodes.title: Tubes are dense in specialization fibres for constructibly Jacobson diamonds
nodes.statement: If (F, D) is a smelted kimberlite with D a cJ-diamond and S ⊂ |F^red| is constructible (locally closed), then |D ∩ F̂_{/S}| = |D^⊚_{/S}| is dense in sp_D^{-1}(S).
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
proofSteps: |D^⊚_{/S}| is the largest generization-stable subset of sp_D^{-1}(S) (D11/tubular-neighbourhood).

sp_D^{-1}(S) is patch-open (sp_D is patch-continuous, D11/specialization-spectral), so rank-one points are dense in it; rank-one points are generization-stable (they have no proper generizations), hence lie in the tube.

nodes.title: Diamonds with enough facets
nodes.statement: For a perfectoid field C of characteristic p, a locally spatial diamond X over Spa(C, O_C) has enough facets if it has a v-cover ⨿_i Spd(A_i, A_i°) → X with each A_i topologically of finite type over C itself. Having enough facets is stable under base change to perfectoid extensions C → C' and fibre products over Spa(C, O_C), implies cJ, and holds for Spd(A, A°) with A smooth topologically of finite type over an untilt C^♯.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4.
