proofSteps: Stability: topologically finite type is stable under completed tensor products and field extension.
cJ: D11/constructibly-jacobson-diamond (surjective images and tft case).

Smooth case: étale locally map to a torus, pull back along the perfectoid torus and use invariance of the étale site under tilting (ECD Lemma 15.6) to cover by Spd of tft algebras over C (Gleason Proposition 4.51).

nodes.title: Specialization of a rich smelted kimberlite is a quotient map
nodes.statement: If K = (F, D) is a rich smelted kimberlite then sp_D : |D| → |F^red| is a quotient map.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
proofSteps: The statement is local on |F^red|; reduce to F^red = Spec A with finitely many irreducible components (local noetherianity).

Irreducible case: take r ∈ |D| over the generic point g, formalizable by Spa(C, O_C) → D; let C_min be the minimal ring of integral elements of C with C_min/C°° ⊇ A; Spa(C, C_min) → (F^red)^{⋄/◦} lifts to D by valuativity.

|Spa(C, C_min)| → |F^red| is specializing, surjective and spectral between spectral spaces, hence closed (DiamondsAndVStacks D0/closure-of-pro-constructible), hence a quotient map; it factors through sp_D, which is therefore a quotient map; finitely many components are handled the same way.

nodes.title: Gleason's connected-components theorem
nodes.statement: Let K = (F,D) be a topologically normal rich smelted kimberlite. Assume also that every point of |F^red| specializes to a closed point. Then π₀(sp_D) : π₀(|D|) → π₀(|F^red|) is bijective. The added condition holds when the reduction has the underlying space of a locally noetherian scheme, in particular a perfection of a scheme locally of finite type over a field.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).

Closed-specialization condition: for each y ∈ |F^red| there is a closed point x with y specializing to x. This is used explicitly in the suggested Lean topological core. The unrestricted formulation in Gleason Lemma 4.55 remains the recorded gap E10; local noetherianity of the underlying topology alone does not supply this condition.
proofSteps: Surjectivity of sp_D gives surjectivity on connected components. For a clopen partition |D| = U ⊔ V, each image is stable under specialization because sp_D is specializing and U,V are closed.

If the two images meet, use the closed-specialization condition to choose a common closed specialization x. Local noetherianity of the underlying topology makes {x} constructible. Tube density and topological normality make sp_D^{-1}(x) connected, contradicting the partition. Thus every clopen subset of |D| is saturated under sp_D.

Apply D11/rich-quotient-theorem: saturated clopens descend to clopens of |F^red|. To pass from clopens to actual connected components, use that a locally noetherian space is locally connected and its components are open. Restrict to the open preimage of each base component; any disconnection there gives a clopen in |D|, whose descended partition would disconnect that base component. Each such preimage is therefore connected, giving injectivity on π₀.
acceptance: For a flat normal formal scheme 𝔛 topologically of finite type over Spf O with k algebraically closed, π₀(𝔛_η) = π₀(𝔛_red), the classical fact recovered here.

Non-example: for 𝔛 = Spf Z_p⟨x, y⟩/(x(x − p)) the generic fibre is two disjoint closed discs while the reduction A¹_{F_p} is connected; the pair is rich but not topologically normal and π₀(sp) is not injective.

nodes.title: Normal formal schemes give topologically normal rich kimberlites
nodes.statement: Let 𝔛 be a separated flat normal formal scheme topologically of finite type over Spf O_E. Then 𝔛^♢ is a flat π-adic kimberlite, and the smelted kimberlite (𝔛^♢, 𝔛^♢_η) is rich and topologically normal; its tube at a closed point x is the diamond of the connected rigid space Spf(Ô_{𝔛,x})^rig. Consequently sp induces a bijection π₀(𝔛^rig) ≅ π₀(𝔛_red).
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
E/Q_p complete discretely valued with perfect residue field k. Topologically of finite type makes 𝔛^♢ formally adic over Spd O_E, so its analytic locus is its generic fibre.
proofSteps: Richness: valuative by D11/valuative-prekimberlite; 𝔛^♢_η is the diamond of an adic space topologically of finite type over E, cJ by Huber's density theorem (D11/constructibly-jacobson-diamond); 𝔛_red is locally of finite type over k; 𝔛^♢ is a flat π-adic kimberlite (D11/flat-pi-adic-kimberlite, finite-type case), so sp is surjective.

nodes.title: π-adic prekimberlites and kimberlites over Spd O
nodes.statement: A small v-sheaf X over Spd O is a π-adic prekimberlite if it is v-locally formal, X → Spd O is separated and formally adic, and X^red is represented by a perfect k-scheme; equivalently X is a prekimberlite with X → Spd O formally adic, in which case X^an = X_η and (X^red)^⋄ = X_s. A π-adic prekimberlite is a π-adic kimberlite if X_η is a locally spatial diamond, sp_X restricted to |X_η| is quasicompact and SP_X is partially proper; equivalently X is a kimberlite formally adic over Spd O. The rule X ↦ (X_η, X^red, sp_X) is functorial, sp_X : |X_η| → |X^red| is spectral when X_η is locally spatial, and closed for π-adic kimberlites.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
O is a complete discrete valuation ring, flat over Z_p, with uniformizer π, fraction field F, perfect residue field k; X_η = X ×_{Spd O} Spd F and X_s = X ×_{Spd O} Spd k.

nodes.title: Flat π-adic kimberlites
nodes.statement: A π-adic kimberlite X over Spd O is flat if it has a v-cover ⨿_i Spd(R_i^{♯+}) → X over Spd O with (R_i^♯, R_i^{♯+}) perfectoid pairs over F. If A → B is a map of π-adically complete flat O-algebras with A integrally closed in A[1/π] and Spd(B[1/π], B) → Spd(A[1/π], A) a v-cover, then Spd(B) → Spd(A) is a v-cover; in particular Spd(A) is a flat π-adic kimberlite for such A, and Spd(A) is flat for A the π-adic completion of a flat O-algebra of finite type. For a flat π-adic kimberlite sp : |X_η| → |X^red| is surjective; conversely a π-adic kimberlite proper over Spd O with surjective sp is flat.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
O is a complete discrete valuation ring, flat over Z_p, with uniformizer π, fraction field F, perfect residue field k; X_η = X ×_{Spd O} Spd F and X_s = X ×_{Spd O} Spd k.
proofSteps: Cover criterion: Spd(B) → Spd(A) is quasicompact (Gleason Lemma 2.26), so it suffices to check surjectivity on points; on the special fibre reduce to surjectivity of Spa(B/π) → Spa(A/π) (D7/perfect-v-covers) and lift points through the surjective Tate specialization of (A[1/π], A) (AGLR Proposition 2.32).

Finite type case: reduce to A reduced using D10/awn-full-faithfulness (1); the integral closure A' of A in A[1/π] is finite, Spd(A') is flat, and Spd(A') → Spd(A) is a v-cover (AGLR Proposition 2.33).

Surjectivity of sp for flat X from D9/tate-specialization-map on Spd(R^{♯+}); the converse by covering X_η with affinoid perfectoids, formalizing, and extending points by partial properness (AGLR Proposition 2.35).
acceptance: Spd O is flat.

nodes.title: The specialization-triple theorem for π-adic kimberlites
nodes.statement: Let 𝒦 be the full subcategory of v-sheaves over Spd O consisting of flat π-adic kimberlites X, quasicompact and separated over Spd O, such that (1) the Spd C-valued points of X are dense in |X_C| (C a completed algebraic closure of F), (2) X^red is a perfect k-scheme perfectly of finite type, and (3) every section Spd C → X_C formalizes to Spd O_C → X_{O_C}. On 𝒦 the generic-fibre functor X ↦ X_η is faithful and X ↦ (X_η, X^red, sp_{X̆}) is fully faithful, with X̆ = X ×_{Spd O} Spd Ŏ.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).
O is a complete discrete valuation ring, flat over Z_p, with uniformizer π, fraction field F, perfect residue field k; X_η = X ×_{Spd O} Spd F and X_s = X ×_{Spd O} Spd k.
proofSteps: Faithfulness: replace X by a cover Spd(R⁺); the diagonal of Y is formally adic and closed, its pullback along (f, g) is a formally closed subsheaf of Spd(R⁺) with the same generic fibre, hence everything by the argument of D9/unique-formalization.
Fullness: for a map of triples, let Z be the image of a formalizable cover Spd(R⁺) → W = X ×_{Spd O} Y under (g, f ∘ g); Z_η is the graph of f_η.
Z is v-locally formal and separated; using density of C-points and formalization of C-sections, the special fibre of Z lies in the graph of f^red, so Z is formally π-adic with Z^red ≅ X^red.
Z → X is an isomorphism on generic and special fibres and quasicompact, hence an isomorphism (ECD Lemma 12.5); compose with the projection to Y.
acceptance: For X = Spd O the triple is (Spd F, Spec k, constant map).

sources.match: Defines the category 𝒦 and proves that on it the generic fibre is faithful and the specialization triple is fully faithful.

nodes.title: Normality of weakly normal formal schemes through connected tubes
nodes.statement: Let O be a complete discrete valuation ring flat over Z_p with algebraically closed residue field k and uniformizer π. Let A be a flat, weakly normal, π-adically complete domain topologically of finite type over O, with A[1/π] normal. If the tube at every closed point of Spec(A/π), equivalently the rigid generic fibre of the corresponding complete local formal scheme, is connected, then A is normal. Algebraic closedness is an extra hypothesis correcting AGLR Proposition 2.39; connectedness alone over a merely perfect k is insufficient.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Perf is the category of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with the v-topology; v-sheaves are small v-sheaves on Perf in the sense of DiamondsAndVStacks D4. For a pre-adic space X over Spa(Z_p, Z_p), X^♢ is the v-sheaf of DiamondsAndVStacks D6.6 (marked untilts with a map to X).

O is a complete discrete valuation ring flat over Z_p, with uniformizer π, fraction field F and algebraically closed residue field k. Weak normality excludes a proper finite birational universal-homeomorphism modification by a reduced scheme (SF.0).
proofSteps: Use D9/formal-neighbourhood to identify each tube with the generic fibre of the completion at its closed point. Let B be the normalization of A in A[1/π]; excellence makes B finite, and B[1/π] = A[1/π].

The completion of B over a closed point x decomposes as the product of its complete local factors. Their generic fibres are disjoint, nonempty (flatness and the flat-kimberlite specialization theorem), and have union the tube of A at x. Connectedness gives exactly one point of Spec(B/π) above x.

All these closed residue fields are k because k is algebraically closed. Thus the finite special-fibre map has one geometric point in each closed fibre. The Jacobson/constructibility criterion for finite maps of finite-type k-schemes gives universal injectivity everywhere; integral surjectivity makes it a universal homeomorphism. Together with the generic-fibre isomorphism this makes Spec B → Spec A a finite birational universal homeomorphism.
Weak normality now implies A = B directly. No absolute-weak-normality full-faithfulness theorem is needed.
acceptance: For A = O⟨T⟩ with k algebraically closed, the tubes at closed points are open discs and A is normal.

Non-example: for A = O⟨x, y⟩/(y² − π²x) with p ≠ 2, A[1/π] ≅ F⟨z⟩ (z = y/π, x = z²) is normal but A is not, and accordingly the tube at a closed point x = ā, with ā a nonzero square in k, is two disjoint discs |z ∓ √a| < 1.

The perfect-residue-field boundary fails: take a nontrivial finite unramified extension L/Q_p, B = O_L and A = Z_p + pB. This finite flat complete local domain is weakly normal but not normal, and A[1/p] = L. Its only tube is Spa(L,O_L), which is connected but becomes disconnected after the unramified base extension. This is source issue E9.

sources.match: The normalization-and-tubes argument proves the corrected criterion over algebraically closed k. The perfect-field generality printed in Proposition 2.39 fails for the unramified-order example E9; singleton closed fibres alone do not give purely inseparable residue extensions.

gaps.title: Completed residue fields of a general universal homeomorphism
gaps.detail: Scholze–Weinstein (§10.2, p. 77) assert without proof that in characteristic 0 a universal homeomorphism of analytic adic spaces induces isomorphisms of completed residue fields. This packet proves it for finite morphisms of adic spaces locally of finite type over a nonarchimedean field (D7/residue-fields-of-finite-universal-homeomorphisms), which covers seminormalization and cuspidal normalization (general normalizations need not be universal homeomorphisms), and states SW20 Proposition 10.2.1 under the residue-field hypothesis. gaps.title: Closed specializations in the unrestricted component criterion
gaps.detail: The passage to a common closed specialization in Gleason Lemma 4.55, p. 38, is not justified by Definition 4.52, which only requires the underlying reduction space to be locally noetherian. A perfect scheme can have locally noetherian topology without closed points: remove the closed point from the spectrum of a perfect valuation ring whose prime ideals form an infinite ascending chain with a maximal limit. Its remaining points have finite-chain open neighborhoods. This is a counterexample to the topological inference, not a constructed counterexample to the kimberlite theorem. The packet proves the theorem with an explicit closed-specialization condition. Derive that condition from the other kimberlite axioms, or supply a proof in their absence, before asserting the printed generality.
